domain.title: Positive Classroom Environment
domain.description: Missouri Standard 5 defines the job as building a place where learning happens — environment, engagement, interaction, self-motivation. Not compliance. Not control. Three views of one room: person · structure · relationship.

claims.statement: The teacher uses an understanding of individual/group motivation and behavior to create a learning environment that encourages active engagement in learning, positive social interaction, and self-motivation.

sources.title: Missouri Teacher Standards — Standard 5: Positive Classroom Environment

strands.title: Time, Space & Flow
strands.subtitle: The structure.
strands.description: Shape time, space, and transitions so the class runs smoothly and stays productive.

units.title: Map the hour
units.description: Design a predictable lesson rhythm students can anticipate.

enactment.k2: Transitions are explicitly modeled and rehearsed (songs, signals, practiced routes); very short work cycles.
enactment.grades35: Students manage their own materials and movement within a set structure; longer cycles.
enactment.grades68: Students move between formats (discussion → group → independent) with minimal cueing; teacher designs, students run it.

strands.title: Culture & Belonging
strands.subtitle: The relational field.
strands.description: Build a culture where students belong, trust each other, and want to learn.

units.title: Make belonging structural
units.description: Build in ways every student belongs by default, not by earning it.

enactment.k2: Belonging built through naming, greeting, and daily ritual; simple, concrete repair language.
enactment.grades35: Students take on classroom roles and simple restorative conversations; norms made explicit and revisited.
enactment.grades68: Students co-own norms and lead repair; identity and peer-belonging are central; culture becomes partly student-run.

not_yet_connected.statement: Durable learning reveals itself over time, through what persists; it is built by repeated, spaced practice.

sources.title: The Science of Learning (2nd ed.)
sources.excerpt: Completion of assignments and absence of errors does not necessarily equate to long-lasting learning. There are many strategies which support short-term performance that inflate the appearance of learning without deepening meaningful, longer-lasting learning.
